title: Text-to-Speech Reading Tool
author: Zhiyu
excerpt: Of all sentient beings in the Saha world, the ear faculty is the keenest. Reading while listening is often easier to understand and remember than reading alone. Therefore you can use a text-to-speech reading tool to read the study materials aloud, listening while you read. Moreover, you can also soak yourself in them through repeated listening.

inline.s: Of all sentient beings in the Saha world, the ear faculty is the keenest. Reading while listening is often easier to understand and remember than reading alone. Therefore you can use a text-to-speech reading tool to read the study materials aloud, listening while you read. Moreover, you can also soak yourself in them through repeated listening.

The text-to-speech reading tool is a tool that helps us study. Like any other tool, the more often you use it, the more skilled you become, the more pronounced the results, and the more precisely you apply it. If you are not familiar with installing and configuring software, you can ask a skilled friend to help, and you need only use it.
There are many text-to-speech programs; for example, “ReaderGirl” is a simple, easy-to-use, and free text-to-speech program. The method of using “ReaderGirl” is described below:

In the process of listening while reading, the text you look at may, according to each person’s preference, be one of the following:

blocks.text: (1) Reading the Text on the Web Page

inline.s: You can have “ReaderGirl” read aloud, while you read the text on the web page.
You can also, while “ReaderGirl” reads aloud, read the text in the “ReaderGirl” editor.
If you like, as when watching a disc, to have the read content displayed sentence by sentence, then click “Read” on the “ReaderGirl” menu, and then click “Turn desktop subtitles
on or off” and it is done. (If later you want to turn the desktop subtitles off, do the same thing once more.)
When the mouse points at the desktop subtitles, a toolbar for setting the subtitles appears; from it you can set the subtitle color, font, whether to use kara
mode, as well as turn the subtitles off.

On a web page, select (highlight) the chapter or paragraph to be read (or right-click the mouse and select all of this text), then right-click and click the “ReaderGirl” icon (or directly click the floating “ReaderGirl” icon), and reading begins. After reading, if you need to read again, you can click the “ReaderGirl” icon again (or directly click the floating “ReaderGirl” icon), and it will read again from the start.
Question: How do I remove the floating “ReaderGirl” icon?
Answer: Click “Settings” in the second row, then click “Basic Settings,” then click the small checkbox before “Show floating reading icon” to deselect it.

A Chinese syllable is formed by a combination of a vowel (final), a consonant (initial), and a tone. Pinyin can be represented by the combination of the above phonetic elements. Tones are marked by the four tone symbols placed above the vowel. In the user dictionary editor, tones are represented by numbers and placed after the vowel.
You can click to input among the following vowels:
iang, iong, uang, ang, eng, ong, iao, ian, ing, uai, er, ai, ei, ao, ou, an, en, ia, ie, in, iu, ua, ue, ui, un, uo, ve, a, o, e, i, u, v.
You can click to input among the following consonants.
b, p, m, f, d, t, n, l, zh, ch, sh, z, c, s, r, j, q, x, g, k, h, y, w
